audience.programmeDescription: Modern Greek Language and Culture at the University of Amsterdam combines Modern Greek language learning with the literature, history and societies of Greece and Cyprus. Students work with Greek cultural sources and study the region’s relationships with Europe and the Mediterranean.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in literature, ancient Greek culture, comparative history, European politics and humanities research. UCR’s courses do not provide sustained study of modern Greece and Cyprus through language, literature, history or regional politics. The Greek content is concentrated in antiquity and comparative examples.

componentNotes.grk-130120116y: The first year also requires a Dutch writing diagnostic. Tutoring continues throughout the programme. These requirements carry no credits.
componentNotes.grk-130221106y: Students need Modern Greek at A2 level. The first-year language courses prepare for reading and discussing Greek literary texts.
componentNotes.grk-130221008y: This example uses the Athens exchange route. The 30 EC combines 12 EC of language study at B1 or above with 18 EC in regional subjects. The course recommends at least 54 EC of year one and attendance in the first semester of year two. An approved home programme is available.
componentNotes.grk-130221086y: Students must command Modern Greek and Dutch at B1 level. The course uses Greek journalistic texts to study Greece, Cyprus and Europe.
componentNotes.grk-approved-free-profiling-space: Use this 30 EC for a minor or an approved combination of electives, a placement or study abroad.
componentNotes.grk-130219002y: Complete the first and second years before starting the thesis. The individual study is written in Dutch or English and includes an oral presentation.
